text:
A design's page sometimes gets swapped for a single piece of it: the whole design surface, or just the design bar, fills the page. It happens while typing in the message box or after "Start with this". It's happened on a new design and on an existing design that was merged into main, so it no longer has a branch.

Likely cause (server/main.js, the /d/ routing, around lines 648–666): a design with no branch is served from the project's own address. The first POST (the draft kept while typing, or Start with this) makes its branch, and after that every GET there is redirected to the worktree's address. When a region reloads its fragment (the surface on design-changed, #design-bar's …/preview/bar on files-changed), the answer comes back from another address, outside the region's scope. Koda routes it by scope, so #main (ko-scope="/") takes it.

Fix: answer a fragment GET there in place (handleDesign with the worktree, as POSTs already are) instead of redirecting. Also, keeping a draft (…/draft, which is saved only on this computer) shouldn't make a branch. While you're in there, check whether "New session" not working is the same redirect.

Full notes: the open question in prelude/design-workspace/NOTES.md.

2970 ## Redirects 2971 2972 **Redirects are the browser's, and they work.** `fetch` follows them, so a 2973 region sees only the response at the end of the chain, and the URL it came from 2974 is what decides where the content lands. 2975 2976 The thing worth knowing is that **`x-koda-fragment: 1` survives the redirect**. 2977 The header is sent again on every hop, so the handler at the far end knows the 2978 request began in a region and can answer with a fragment rather than a page. 2979 Nothing has to be threaded through a query string, and no marker has to be 2980 returned in a body for the client to follow itself. 2981 2982 ### Post, redirect, get 2983 2984 ``` 2985 POST /app/orders → 303 See Other, Location: /app/orders/1041 2986 GET /app/orders/1041 →

saved as ORD-1041

2987 ``` 2988 2989 The fragment is attached, and **the address bar becomes `/app/orders/1041`** if 2990 the landing region owns history. That is the whole point of the pattern: the 2991 result of a save has a URL of its own, so reloading or sharing the page shows 2992 the saved thing rather than whatever was there before. 2993 2994 An un-redirected `POST` records nothing, because its URL is an action rather 2995 than a place, and offering a reload that re-runs the save is what 2996 post-redirect-get exists to avoid. 2997 2998 | | Attached | Recorded in history | 2999 |---|---|---| 3000 | `GET` | yes | yes | 3001 | `POST` | yes | no | 3002 | `POST` → `303` → `GET` | yes | **yes**, at the final URL | 3003 3004 ### What is not known 3005 3006 Which hops happened. A response says only that it *was* redirected, so `302` and 3007 `303` - which turn a `POST` into a `GET` - cannot be told apart from `307` and 3008 `308`, which preserve the method. Koda treats any redirect as "the result is at 3009 this URL", which is what the first pair mean. 3010 3011 So a `307` or `308` answering a `POST` into a region that owns history would 3012 record a URL that only answers `POST`. I agree with your diagnosis. The code and Koda's reference both support it. One correction: on the design page the region that takes the fragment is `#workspace`, not `#main`. New session is probably a separate problem.

**Why the page gets swapped**
- `server/main.js:648–666`: in a repository, a design with no branch is found on the project's own folder. A POST makes its branch first (`branchFor`, line 657) and is answered in place with the worktree (line 665). Once the branch exists, every GET at the project's address gets a redirect to `/f/<worktree>/…` (line 662).
- Both POSTs you named go through this path, and neither needs a branch:
  - Keeping the draft while typing: `POST …/draft`, line 1576. It's saved under `~/.prelude/drafts/<folder.id>/…` (`server/drafts.js:53`).
  - Start with this: `POST …/start`, line 1524. It only writes the draft as well.
- The regions that reload get their scope from their own address:
  - The surface: `server/views/_surface.eta:43` has `ko-source`/`ko-location` set to its preview URL and reloads on `design-changed`.
  - `#design-bar` (`_surface.eta:51`) reloads `…/preview/bar` on `files-changed`.
- Koda follows the redirect and routes by the address it ends at. The reference (`reference.md:2972–2974`, "Redirects") says the URL the response came from "is what decides where the content lands", and the most specific scope wins (`:2171`). The worktree address isn't under the region's scope, so the only match is `#workspace ko-scope="/"` (`server/views/layout.eta:17`). In the pop-out window it's `#main` (`window-layout.eta:11`). Either way, the whole page becomes the surface or the bar.

**Something else the redirect causes:** the page's live channel (`${base}/live`, line 1283) was opened on the project's address. Its key is `designKey(folder, design)` (`server/turns.js:41`), and changes are watched in the project folder's design directory (line 1490). Once the branch exists, the agent works in the worktree, so the page doesn't hear those events. When the EventSource reconnects, it's redirected to the worktree's channel, and the next event sets off a reload that gets swapped. That's probably why it only happens "sometimes".

**New session** probably isn't the same redirect. The link (`server/views/_chat.eta:25`) is a plain `<a>` in `#workspace`, whose scope is `/`. A redirected answer would still land in `#workspace`, which is the right region. `GET …/sessions/new` is answered at line 2415 (the NOTES' `:2240` is out of date). One guess: on a page that already shows a new session (`it.session` null, which `GET …/d/<design>` gives when the last session is finished), New session is the current item, and clicking it reloads the same empty session. It needs reproducing: what the request returns and which region takes it.

**What I'd change (on a branch)**
- `server/main.js:661–662`: answer in place with `handleDesign` on the worktree for a fragment GET (`x-koda-fragment: 1`) and for the `…/live` channel. Keep the redirect only for a cold page load, so the address bar still moves.
- `server/main.js:656`: don't make the branch for posts that only change the draft (`…/draft`, `…/sessions/<id>/draft`, `…/start`, `…/questions/<id>/answer`).
- When a branch is made, move the draft with `app.drafts.move(folder, design, worktree, design)`. Drafts are keyed by folder id, and Send reads them from the worktree (`messageOf`, line 2425). Without the move, images kept before the branch existed would be dropped.
- `prelude/design-workspace/NOTES.md`: once fixed, turn the open question into a decision, and fix the line number in the New session question.
Fixing this on prelude/fix-a-design-s-page-sometimes-gets-swapped-for-a-singl, made from main. The agent can change the project there now; each turn is committed to the branch.
Carry on

I've fixed it in the app, along the lines you suggested. I couldn't run anything, so the tests are written but haven't been run yet.

**What changed** (`server/main.js`, the `/d/` routing)
- **Region reloads stay on the page.** When a design has a branch, a region reloading itself at the project's address is now answered right there, from the branch's worktree. That covers the surface after the agent's changes and the design bar. Only a fresh page load is still sent on to the worktree's address. The surface or bar no longer comes back from another address, so it stays in its own place instead of filling the page.
- **Keeping a draft no longer makes a branch.** Saving what's typed, Start with this, answering a question, and adding, removing or marking up images in the tray all only touch the draft saved on this computer. A new function, `changesDraftOnly`, picks these out.
- **The draft moves when a branch is made.** Drafts are saved per project folder, and Send reads them from the worktree. Without the move, what you'd typed (and any images) before the branch existed would disappear from the box when you sent. Now another post that makes the branch, such as sending a message, moves the draft with it.

None of this changes how any page looks, so no design's views, styles or states changed.

**Notes**
- In `prelude/design-workspace/NOTES.md`, the open question is now a decision.
- The fix's own notes are in `prelude/fixes/a-design-s-page-sometimes-gets-swapped-for-a-single-piece/NOTES.md`.

**New session** is still an open question, and I've corrected its line reference in the design's notes. It probably isn't the same redirect: the link sits in the region that owns the whole page, so even a redirected answer would land in the right place. It needs reproducing to see what happens when it's clicked.

**Tests:** I added one to `test/app.test.js` ("a design with no branch keeps its draft without one…"). It checks that:
- saving a draft and Start with this make no branch;
- the next post makes the branch and moves the draft;
- a fresh page load still redirects;
- a region's reload is answered in place.

Run `node --test test/app.test.js`, then `node --test` for the whole suite, paying particular attention to `chat.test.js` and `preview.test.js`.

**To check in the app**
1. Open a design that was merged into main. Type in the box and use Start with this: no `prelude/<design>` branch should appear.
2. Send a message to make the branch, and let the agent change the design. The surface and the bar should update in place without taking over the page.
